mainTopic: The text of the wedding blessings, when and how they are said, and who counts toward the ten.
overview: This amud finishes the text of the ברכת חתנים, the six wedding blessings that, together with the blessing over the wine, make up the seven blessings. The גמרא then tells of לוי saying five blessings and רב אסי saying six. It explains the difference through the creation of man: everyone agrees man was created once, but one view follows ה׳'s first thought to create two, and the other follows the act. Next come practical rules. All the blessings are said on later days only when there are פנים חדשות. The גמרא also sets how long שהשמחה במעונו is said, from when wedding preparations begin until twelve months after the wedding, and brings stories about רב פפא and רבינא blessing from אירוסין. The הלכה does not follow רב תחליפא's long blessings, and it does not follow רב חביבא's saying שהשמחה במעונו at a ברית מילה. Finally, רב and רבי יוחנן rule that חתנים count toward the ten but אבלים do not. A ברייתא challenges both. רב is defended as having the standing of a תנא, and the answer for רבי יוחנן comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The end of the first blessing: All was created for His glory
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the first wedding blessing, which praises ה׳ for creating everything for His glory.
steps.simpleTranslation: [Blessed are You... King of the universe,] Who created everything for His glory.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the first of the wedding blessings in רב יהודה's list. The opening words of this blessing came just before this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a short blessing with no closing line. It praises ה׳ for creating the whole world for His honor. That idea fits a wedding, where people gather to honor the חתן and כלה.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessings said at a wedding, also called the שבע ברכות
Who created everything for His glory

phrases.english: Who created everything for His glory.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב יהודה's list of the wedding blessings, which began before this point.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first wedding blessing praises ה׳ Who created everything for His glory.

steps.title: The second blessing: Creator of man
steps.stepSummary: The second blessing is a short blessing that praises ה׳ as the Creator of mankind.
steps.simpleTranslation: And [the second blessing is: Blessed are You... ] Creator of man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the next blessing in the list: a short blessing that praises ה׳ as יוצר האדם, the Creator of man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the key words are given here, because the full opening ('Blessed are You... King of the universe') is understood. This blessing praises the creation of אדם הראשון, the first human being.

phrases.english: And 'Creator of man.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next blessing in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The second wedding blessing is a short blessing: Blessed are You... יוצר האדם.

steps.title: The third blessing: Man made in God's image, and the building from him
steps.stepSummary: The third blessing is longer. It praises ה׳ for making man in His image and for forming a lasting 'building' (woman) out of him. It also closes with יוצר האדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And [the third blessing is: Blessed are You...] Who made man in His image, in the image of the likeness of His form, and prepared for him, out of himself, an everlasting building. Blessed are You, ה׳, Creator of man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third blessing. It describes man being created in God's image and woman being formed from him, and it ends with the words 'Blessed are You, ה׳, Creator of man.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the short blessing before it, this one has a full closing line (חתימה). The 'building' comes from בראשית 2:22, where חוה is 'built' from אדם's side. That is why this blessing fits a wedding so well: man and woman come from one source and build a lasting family.

keyTerms.meaning: An everlasting building, meaning woman, who builds the family
The closing line of a blessing ('Blessed are You, ה׳...')

steps.confusionAlert: Two blessings in a row end with יוצר האדם. The second one is short (step 2), and this third one is long with a full closing line. They are separate blessings, not the same one repeated.
steps.whyThisMatters: Right after this list, the גמרא brings a debate about whether five or six blessings are said, and whether man was created in one act of creation or two. The two separate יוצר האדם blessings are the background for that debate.

phrases.english: And 'Who made man in His image,'
in the image of the likeness of His form,
and prepared for him, out of himself,
phrases.notes: Woman was formed from the man himself, from his side.

phrases.english: an everlasting building.
Blessed are You, Lord, Creator of man.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next blessing in the list. It closes with the same words as the short blessing before it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The third wedding blessing praises the creation of man in God's image and of woman from him, closing with יוצר האדם.

steps.title: The fourth blessing: The joy of ציון when her children return
steps.stepSummary: The fourth blessing prays that ירושלים, pictured as a barren woman, will rejoice when her children are gathered back into her. It closes: Who gladdens ציון through her children.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'May the barren one greatly rejoice and be glad, with the gathering of her children into her in joy. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who gladdens ציון through her children.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the fourth blessing, which turns from the wedding couple to ירושלים and prays for her children to come home in joy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'barren one' is ירושלים, which now seems empty and childless because of the גלות. At a moment of personal joy like a wedding, we remember ציון and ask that her children return. The blessing closes with its own חתימה: משמח ציון בבניה.

keyTerms.meaning: Who gladdens ציון through her children

steps.confusionAlert: 'The barren one' here is not the כלה. It refers to ירושלים, which is waiting for her children to return.

phrases.english: 'May the barren one greatly rejoice and be glad,
phrases.notes: 'The barren one' is ירושלים, pictured as a mother without her children.

phrases.english: with the gathering of her children into her in joy.

phrases.aramaic: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳, מְשַׂמֵּחַ צִיּוֹן בְּבָנֶיהָ״.
phrases.english: Blessed are You, Lord, Who gladdens Zion through her children.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next blessing in the list. It shifts the focus from the creation of man to the joy of ציון.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fourth wedding blessing prays for ציון's joy at her children's return, closing משמח ציון בבניה.
steps.whatToRemember: So far the wedding blessings are: שהכל ברא לכבודו, then יוצר האדם (short), then אשר יצר (long, closing יוצר האדם), then שוש תשיש (closing משמח ציון בבניה).

steps.title: The fifth blessing: Gladden the loving friends
steps.stepSummary: The fifth wedding blessing asks ה׳ to give the couple great joy, like the joy He gave His creation in גן עדן. It closes: Who gladdens the חתן and כלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Bring great joy to these loving friends, just as You brought joy to Your creation in גן עדן long ago. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who brings joy to the groom and bride.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the list and gives the wording of the fifth wedding blessing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous blessing spoke about ירושלים and her children. This blessing turns back to the couple standing under the חופה. It compares their joy to the joy ה׳ gave in גן עדן.

keyTerms.meaning: Bring great joy (the doubled verb adds emphasis)
The loving friends, meaning the new couple
Who gives joy to the groom and bride (the closing of this blessing)

phrases.english: Bring great joy to the loving friends,
phrases.notes: The "loving friends" are the חתן and כלה.

phrases.english: as You gave joy to Your creation in the Garden of Eden long ago.

phrases.aramaic: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳, מְשַׂמֵּחַ חָתָן וְכַלָּה״.
phrases.english: Blessed are You, Lord, Who brings joy to the groom and bride.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of wedding blessings with the fifth one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fifth wedding blessing is שמח תשמח, which closes with משמח חתן וכלה.

steps.title: The sixth blessing: Who created joy and gladness
steps.stepSummary: The sixth and longest blessing praises ה׳ for creating joy, the חתן and כלה, and many kinds of happiness. It prays that the sounds of weddings will soon be heard in ירושלים. It closes: Who gladdens the חתן with the כלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Blessed are You, ה׳ our God, King of the world, Who created joy and gladness, groom and bride, delight, song, happiness, cheer, love, brotherhood, peace and friendship. Soon, ה׳ our God, may there be heard in the cities of יהודה and the streets of ירושלים the sound of joy and gladness, the sound of groom and bride, the happy sound of grooms from their חופה and young people from their feast of song. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who makes the groom rejoice with the bride.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the wording of the sixth wedding blessing, which ends the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This blessing begins with praise and lists ten words for joy and closeness. It then prays for the future, using the language of the פסוק in ירמיהו about the sounds of weddings returning to ירושלים. Together with the blessing over the wine, these make up the seven wedding blessings.
steps.whatToRemember: The list is now complete: six blessings about the wedding, plus the blessing over the wine, make seven.
steps.confusionAlert: The two blessings sound alike but end differently. The fifth ends משמח חתן וכלה, and the sixth ends משמח חתן עם הכלה.

phrases.english: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe,

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר בָּרָא שָׂשׂוֹן וְשִׂמְחָה, חָתָן וְכַלָּה,
phrases.english: Who created joy and gladness, groom and bride,
delight, song, happiness, cheer,
love and brotherhood, and peace and friendship.
Soon, Lord our God, may there be heard
in the cities of Judea and in the streets of Jerusalem

phrases.aramaic: קוֹל שָׂשׂוֹן וְקוֹל שִׂמְחָה, קוֹל חָתָן וְקוֹל כַּלָּה,
phrases.english: the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the sound of the groom and the sound of the bride,
the joyous sound of grooms from their wedding canopy
and of young people from their feast of song.

phrases.aramaic: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳, מְשַׂמֵּחַ חָתָן עִם הַכַּלָּה״.
phrases.english: Blessed are You, Lord, Who makes the groom rejoice with the bride.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the sixth and last blessing, which completes the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sixth wedding blessing is אשר ברא, which closes with משמח חתן עם הכלה.

steps.title: Two weddings: one Sage said five blessings, another said six
steps.stepSummary: לוי came to רבי's house for the wedding of רבי שמעון, רבי's son, and said five blessings. רב אסי came to רב אשי's house for the wedding of מר, רב אשי's son, and said six blessings.
steps.simpleTranslation: לוי happened to come to רבי's house at the wedding of רבי's son, רבי שמעון, and he said five blessings. רב אסי happened to come to רב אשי's house at the wedding of רב אשי's son, מר, and he said six blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells two short stories in which great Sages said different numbers of wedding blessings. This sets up the question of why they acted differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full list has six blessings, not counting the wine. רב אסי said all six, but לוי left one out. Steps 8 and 9 explain why, and the reason has to do with the two blessings about creating man.

keyTerms.meaning: Happened to come, chanced upon a place

phrases.english: Levi happened to come to the house of Rabbi
during the wedding celebration of Rabbi Shimon, his son,
and he recited five blessings.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אַסִּי אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב אָשֵׁי
phrases.english: Rav Asi happened to come to the house of Rav Ashi
during the wedding celebration of Mar, his son,
and he recited six blessings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the full list, two stories show that Sages did not all say the same number of blessings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לוי said five wedding blessings, and רב אסי said six.

steps.title: Suggestion: they argue over one creation of man or two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the two Sages disagree about how man was created. One holds it was a single act of creation, so one blessing about creating man is enough. The other holds it was two acts of creation, so two blessings are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that this is what they disagree about? One Sage holds there was one act of creation, and the other holds there were two acts of creation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא makes a first guess to explain why לוי said five blessings and רב אסי said six. The word לימא shows this is only a suggestion, and the גמרא is getting ready to test it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two of the blessings deal with creating man: יוצר האדם and אשר יצר. If man and woman came from a single act of creation, one blessing covers it, so there are five blessings. If there were two acts of creation, each gets its own blessing, so there are six.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? It introduces a guess that may be rejected
An act of forming or creating

steps.confusionAlert: A line that starts with לימא is a guess, not a final answer. Often the גמרא goes on to reject it, so don't treat it as the conclusion yet.
steps.whyThisMatters: It links a practical question, how many wedding blessings to say, to a deeper question about how man and woman were created.

phrases.english: Shall we say that they disagree about this:
that one Sage holds there was one act of creation,
phrases.notes: Man was created once, with a male and a female side that were later separated.

phrases.english: and one Sage holds there were two acts of creation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible reason for the different numbers of blessings in the two stories.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Suggested reason: the person who said five holds one creation of man, and the person who said six holds two creations.

steps.title: Both agree on one act of creation; they argue about thought versus action
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that the two Sages argue about one creation or two. Everyone agrees there was one act of creation. One Sage follows ה׳'s original thought, and the other follows what ה׳ actually did.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, everyone agrees there was one act of creation. One Sage holds we go after the thought, and the other holds we go after the action.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own suggestion from the last step. It offers a different way to understand the argument between לוי and רב אסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the argument was about what actually happened: one creation or two. Now the facts are agreed: one creation. The argument becomes which counts for the blessings, ה׳'s first plan (two, so six blessings) or the final act (one, so five blessings).

keyTerms.meaning: We go after the thought (the original plan)
We go after the action (what actually happened)

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees
that it was one act of creation.
One Sage holds we go after the thought,
phrases.notes: This fits the one who said six blessings, since the first thought was to create two.

phrases.english: and the other Sage holds we go after the action.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 8's explanation of the argument and replaces it with a new one
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the Sages disagree about the facts of how man was created
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument need not be about the facts. Both can agree on one creation and still argue about whether the thought or the action decides the blessings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One creation in fact; the argument is whether thought or action determines the number of blessings

steps.title: רב יהודה shows the first thought was two but one was created
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה points out two פסוקים that seem to contradict each other. One says man was created in His image, which sounds like one. The other says male and female He created them, which sounds like two. He answers that the first thought was two, but in the end one was created.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רב יהודה asked. One פסוק says, 'And God created man in His image.' Another says, 'Male and female He created them.' How can both be true? At first the plan was to create two, and in the end one was created.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from רב יהודה. It shows there really was a 'thought' of two and an 'action' of one, which is the basis for the explanation in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 only works if ה׳'s thought and His action were actually different. רב יהודה's answer to the two פסוקים shows exactly that: two in thought, one in deed. So both Sages are reading the same facts and just choosing a different stage to follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Points out a contradiction (between two sources)
How can this be? (how do both fit together)
It arose in thought, meaning it was the plan

phrases.english: This is like what רב יהודה pointed out as a contradiction:
It is written: "And God created man in His image,"
and it is written: "Male and female He created them."
How can this be?
At first the thought arose to create two,
and in the end one was created.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 9 by showing that thought and action really differed in man's creation
steps.raayaObject: The idea that ה׳'s plan (two) and His act (one) were different
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה's resolution of the contradiction between בראשית 1:27 and בראשית 5:2
steps.whatToRemember: Both Sages agree man was created as one. The six-blessing view counts ה׳'s first thought of two, and the five-blessing view counts the actual act of one.

steps.title: רב אשי says all the blessings only when new faces come
steps.stepSummary: At רב כהנא's house, רב אשי said all the blessings on the first day. After that, he said them all only if new faces were present. Otherwise, he said only שהשמחה במעונו and אשר ברא, since the meal was just more of the same celebration.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי came to רב כהנא's house. On the first day he said all the blessings. After that, if new faces were there, he said all of them. If not, he said it was just adding to the joy, so he said only 'In Whose dwelling is joy' and 'Who created.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a practical story about how the wedding blessings are said during the days after the wedding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The full set of blessings is for the first day, or when new people come and the celebration is new for them. Without new faces, the meal only continues the joy that already exists. So only two blessings are said.

keyTerms.meaning: New faces (guests who were not there before)
"In Whose dwelling is joy," added to the זימון at a wedding meal

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב כָּהֲנָא.
phrases.english: רב אשי happened to come to רב כהנא's house.
On the first day he said all of them,

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ אִי אִיכָּא פָּנִים חֲדָשׁוֹת —
phrases.english: from then on, if there were new faces,
he said all of them,
and if not,
it is just adding to the joy,
so he says "In Whose dwelling is joy" and "Who created."
phrases.notes: "Who created" is the sixth blessing from step 6.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the creation discussion and gives practical practice for the days after the wedding
steps.mimraCoreRuling: First day: all blessings. Later days: all blessings only with new faces; otherwise only שהשמחה במעונו and אשר ברא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the practice that שבע ברכות on later days need פנים חדשות.

steps.title: When שהשמחה במעונו is said from day seven onward
steps.stepSummary: From the seventh day until the thirtieth, שהשמחה במעונו is said whether or not the חתן said the meal was for the wedding. After thirty days, it is said only if he said the meal was for the wedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: From seven until thirty days, whether or not he told the guests the meal was for the wedding, he says 'In Whose dwelling is joy.' After that, if he told them it was for the wedding, he says it; if not, he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the rule for שהשמחה במעונו after the first week of the wedding has ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the first thirty days, any meal the חתן makes is assumed to be part of the wedding joy. After thirty days, that is no longer assumed. He must say outright that the meal is for the wedding.

phrases.english: From seven until thirty,
phrases.notes: He means days after the wedding.

phrases.english: whether he told them it is because of the wedding,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין לָא אָמַר לְהוּ מֵחֲמַת הִלּוּלָא —
phrases.english: or he did not tell them it is because of the wedding,
he says "In Whose dwelling is joy."
From then on,
if he told them it is because of the wedding,
he says "In Whose dwelling is joy,"
and if not, he does not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the practical rules, now for the time after the first week
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Days 7 to 30: always say שהשמחה במעונו. After 30: only if the meal was called a wedding meal.

steps.title: Until when can a meal still count as a wedding meal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how long the חתן can keep calling a meal a wedding meal so that שהשמחה במעונו is said.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he tells them it is because of the wedding, until when does this work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question about the rule it just gave. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said that after thirty days, saying 'it is for the wedding' allows the blessing. But that cannot go on forever, so the גמרא wants the outer limit.

phrases.english: And when he tells them it is because of the wedding,
until when?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אָמַר לְהוּ מֵחֲמַת הִלּוּלָא, עַד אֵימַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the time limit on step 12's rule
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The latest time a meal can be called a wedding meal for שהשמחה במעונו

steps.title: Up to twelve months
steps.stepSummary: רב פפי, in the name of רבא, answers that it works for twelve months after the wedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפי said in the name of רבא: until twelve months of the year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 13 by giving a limit of one year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a full year after the wedding, a meal that the חתן says is for the wedding still counts as wedding joy. After that, the blessing is no longer said.

phrases.english: רב פפי said in the name of רבא:
Until twelve months of the year.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Up to twelve months after the wedding

steps.title: From when does the blessing begin before the wedding?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the opposite question: before the wedding, from when may שהשמחה במעונו start being said?
steps.simpleTranslation: And at the beginning, from when?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the end point is known, the גמרא asks about the starting point. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wedding joy has an end, twelve months. The גמרא now wants to know when that joy begins, before the wedding itself.

keyTerms.meaning: At the beginning, from the start

phrases.english: And at the beginning, from when?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 13, asking about the start instead of the end
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The earliest time before the wedding that שהשמחה במעונו may be said

steps.title: From when they start preparing the wedding beer
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that it begins from when they put barley into the mortar to make beer for the wedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: from when they throw barley into the mortar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 15. The joy begins once actual wedding preparations start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The start is tied to a real, visible preparation for the feast, making the beer. That is when the house is already busy with the coming wedding.

phrases.english: רב פפא said:
From when they throw barley into the mortar.
phrases.notes: This is the barley being crushed to brew beer for the wedding feast.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מִכִּי רְמוּ שְׂעָרֵי בַּאֲסִינְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From when barley is put in the mortar to brew the wedding beer

steps.title: But רב פפא himself said it from the betrothal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: at his son אבא מר's wedding, he said the blessing already from the time of אירוסין, which is earlier than the barley stage.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב פפא made the match for his son אבא מר, and he said the blessing from the time of the betrothal!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא's rule using his own actions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא said the blessing starts when the beer is prepared. Yet he himself started earlier, at אירוסין. His practice seems to go against his own rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Betrothal, the first stage of marriage

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא רַב פָּפָּא אִיעֲסַק לְאַבָּא מָר בְּרֵיהּ,
phrases.english: But רב פפא arranged the marriage for אבא מר his son,
and he said the blessing from the time of the betrothal!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 16 from רב פפא's own practice
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's rule that the blessing begins from the barley stage
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own practice of blessing from אירוסין is earlier than his stated starting point

steps.title: רב פפא was different because everything was already prepared
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב פפא's case was special. The wedding preparations were already done for him, so the joy began from the betrothal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא is different, because it was already prepared for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that רב פפא's case was an exception, not a change to his rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule ties the start of the joy to the start of preparations. For רב פפא, the preparations were already finished at the betrothal, so his joy began then. The rule stays the same; only the facts of his case were different.

phrases.english: רב פפא is different,
because it was already prepared for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא's practice contradicts his rule about the barley
steps.terutzMaskana: His rule stands. In his case preparations were already complete, so the joy began at אירוסין.
steps.whatToRemember: שהשמחה במעונו is said from when wedding preparations begin until twelve months after the wedding. After thirty days, it is said only if the meal is called a wedding meal.

steps.title: רבינא blesses from betrothal, and the match falls apart
steps.stepSummary: רבינא said the blessing from the time of אירוסין because he was sure the other family would not back out, but they did back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא arranged for his son to marry into the family of רב חביבא, and he said the blessing already from the time of אירוסין. He said: I am sure about them that they will not back out. But it did not work out, and they backed out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about someone else who started the blessing early, at אירוסין, like רב פפא did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא could start at אירוסין because the wedding preparations were already done. רבינא started early for a different reason: he was sure the match would hold. The story shows that being sure is not enough, because his match was cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: they back out / take back their commitment
the matter did not work out

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with רב פפא in Step 18. His early blessing worked because the preparations were ready. רבינא relied only on feeling sure, and it failed.

phrases.aramaic: רָבִינָא אִיעֲסַק לֵיהּ לִבְרֵיהּ בֵּי רַב חֲבִיבָא,
phrases.english: Ravina arranged a match for his son with the house of Rav Chaviva,
and he recited the blessing from the time of betrothal.
phrases.notes: The blessing here is שהשמחה במעונו, the one the גמרא has been discussing.

phrases.english: He said: I am certain about them
that they will not back out.
The matter did not work out
and they backed out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second case of blessing from אירוסין. Unlike רב פפא's case, this one failed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Feeling sure that a match will hold is not a reliable reason to start the blessing at אירוסין.

steps.title: רב תחליפא says six long blessings in בבל
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא came from ארץ ישראל to בבל and said six long wedding blessings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא from the West came to בבל, and he said six long blessings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about a visitor who said the wedding blessings in a longer form. It is setting up the ruling that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story is about the wording and length of the wedding blessings. רב תחליפא made them long. The very next line tells us whether this is correct.

phrases.english: Rav Tachlifa from the West
phrases.notes: "The West" is how people in בבל referred to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: happened to come to Babylonia,
he recited six long blessings.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר מַעְרְבָא אִיקְּלַע לְבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from when the blessing is said to how it is worded.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story: רב תחליפא said six long wedding blessings.

steps.title: The הלכה does not follow רב תחליפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rules that we do not follow רב תחליפא's long blessings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is not like him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its ruling on the story: we do not say the blessings the way רב תחליפא did.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story alone could make it look acceptable to make the blessings longer. This ruling tells us not to. We keep the standard wording of the blessings.

keyTerms.meaning: and the הלכה is not like him

phrases.english: And the halacha is not in accordance with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling on the story in Step 20.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Do not say the wedding blessings in the long form רב תחליפא used.

steps.title: רב חביבא says the joy blessing at a ברית מילה
steps.stepSummary: רב חביבא visited a ברית מילה and said שהשמחה במעונו there.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חביבא came to a house where there was a ברית מילה, and he said the blessing "in Whose dwelling is joy."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story, this time about using the wedding blessing at a ברית מילה. It is setting up the ruling that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שהשמחה במעונו is part of the wedding blessings. רב חביבא used it at a ברית מילה because that is also a happy occasion. The question is whether that is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: a house where a ברית מילה is taking place
"in Whose dwelling is joy", a phrase added to the blessing at a wedding

phrases.english: Rav Chaviva happened to come to a house of a circumcision,
he recited "in Whose dwelling is joy."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story that takes the wedding blessing to a different happy event.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Story: רב חביבא said שהשמחה במעונו at a ברית מילה.

steps.title: No joy blessing at a circumcision, because the baby is in pain
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה does not follow רב חביבא, because the parents are worried about the baby's pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is not like him, because they are anxious, since the baby is in pain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rules against רב חביבא and gives its reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברית מילה is a happy event, but the joy is not complete. The parents are worried because the baby is in pain. So a blessing that celebrates joy does not fit there.
steps.whatToRemember: שהשמחה במעונו is not said at a ברית מילה, because the baby's pain keeps the joy from being complete.

phrases.english: And the halacha is not in accordance with him
because they are anxious
since the baby is in pain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling and the reason for the story in Step 22.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Do not say שהשמחה במעונו at a ברית מילה.

steps.title: רב: grooms count toward the ten, mourners do not
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes רב: חתנים are counted in the ten, but אבלים are not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רב: grooms are counted in the number, and mourners are not counted in the number.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: who may be counted in the group of ten needed for these blessings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some blessings need ten men present. רב says a חתן counts toward that ten. An אבל does not count toward the ten needed for the mourners' blessing.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said that Rav said:
Grooms are counted in the number,
phrases.notes: "The number" means the ten men needed to say the blessings.

phrases.english: and mourners are not counted in the number.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: who counts toward the ten.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חתנים count toward the ten. אבלים do not.

steps.title: A ברייתא says אבלים do count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב from a ברייתא that says both חתנים and אבלים count.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: grooms and mourners are counted in the number!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's rule with an older teaching that disagrees with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא agrees with רב about חתנים. It disagrees about אבלים: it says they do count. Normally a later teacher cannot argue with a ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: they raised an objection (from an older source)

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Grooms and mourners are counted in the number!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's rule about אבלים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that אבלים do not count toward the ten.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says אבלים do count, and an אמורא normally cannot argue with a ברייתא.

steps.title: רב has the status of a תנא and may disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב counts as a תנא, so he is allowed to disagree with a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you raising a ברייתא against רב? רב is a תנא, and he may disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. He is allowed to argue with the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that רב must follow every ברייתא. The answer is that רב has the special standing of a תנא. So he may hold a different view about אבלים.

keyTerms.meaning: a teaching from the time of the תנאים, here a ברייתא
רב is a תנא and may disagree

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that רב has the standing of a תנא, comes up throughout ש״ס whenever a ברייתא seems to contradict רב.

phrases.english: Are you raising a baraita against Rav?
Rav is a tanna, and he disagrees.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in Step 25.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the speaker authority: רב has the standing of a תנא and may disagree with a ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed רב, as an אמורא, must follow the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב may disagree with the ברייתא, so his rule stands.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן holds the same rule
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק quotes רבי יוחנן with the same rule: חתנים count, אבלים do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן: grooms are counted in the number, and mourners are not counted in the number.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the same rule from רבי יוחנן. It is setting up the same challenge against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is the same as רב's. The difference is who said it: רבי יוחנן is not treated as a תנא. So the answer that saved רב will not work for him.

keyTerms.meaning: it was stated (introduces a teaching of the אמוראים)

phrases.aramaic: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: It was stated: Rabbi Yitzchak said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Grooms are counted in the number,
and mourners are not counted in the number.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the same rule as Step 24, from a different teacher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן also holds that חתנים count and אבלים do not.

steps.title: The same ברייתא challenges רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא raises the same ברייתא against רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: grooms and mourners are counted in the number!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן with the same ברייתא it used against רב. Here the answer "he is a תנא" is not available.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words of the challenge are the same as in Step 25. But now the target is רבי יוחנן, who cannot argue with a ברייתא. So the answer that saved רב does not work here; the גמרא's response comes on the next amud.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a pointless repeat of Step 25. The same words now hit a different teacher, and the old answer no longer works.

phrases.english: They raised an objection: Grooms and mourners are counted in the number!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי יוחנן's rule from Step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that אבלים do not count toward the ten.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says אבלים count, and רבי יוחנן, unlike רב, cannot simply disagree with a ברייתא.
